properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-18, asking whether Tim Kellogg's "MCP is unnecessary" (https://timkellogg.me/blog/2025/04/27/mcp-is-unnecessary) changes anything about how or what reflow2 should and should not do, restating the premise: "reflow2 is designed to partner with an LLM and human, not replace it. If there are things an LLM does better, reflow2 shouldn't try to replace that functionality. The partnership between LLM, human, and graph should be synergistic and help mitigate each other's weaknesses."

═══ WHAT THE ARTICLE ACTUALLY CLAIMS (read 2026-09-18) ═══
MCP has no strong technological justification — a tool declaration is text you could paste into a prompt in JSON, XML or Python; OpenAPI already advertises and calls operations — but it is necessary SOCIOLOGICALLY: "the absolute strongest argument for MCP is that there's mostly only a single way to do things", where OpenAPI leaves POST-vs-PUT ambiguities; and its one technical merit is GRANULARITY, wrapping a start/poll/result sequence into one operation so the model has fewer places to err. Concession: "standards are mostly sociological advancements."

═══ DOES IT CHANGE WHAT REFLOW2 SHOULD OR SHOULD NOT DO? — the finding, not a verdict ═══
The article is about the WIRE and the DECLARATION; Anthony's premise is about the DIVISION OF LABOUR. They are orthogonal: dec:three-party-checks (2026-07-19, "the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides") holds whether reflow2 is reached over MCP, OpenAPI or a CLI, and dec:agent-navigates-content applies it to content. So the article changes nothing about WHAT reflow2 does. It says three things about HOW the surface should look, each of which the design already leans toward and one of which sharpens a criterion:

1. THE DECLARATIONS ARE THE PRODUCT. If a tool declaration is just text the model reads, then the description is not documentation of the tool, it IS the interface — which is what the 2026-09-18 ruling "words before pruning" already acted on (every tool first for its own job), and what the lessons-on-tools mechanism (a design's rules appended to a tool's description) exploits. Counter: reflow2's own instrument found that a dot product over descriptions measures shared prose, not shared job; the words matter, but the corpus of user-phrased jobs is the test, not the words themselves.

2. "ONE WAY TO DO THINGS" IS THE VALUE OF A STANDARD, and reflow2 serves 186 ways. This is the strongest thing the article says against the current surface: every second door for one job spends the exact thing a standard buys. It argues FOR continuing the prune-with-evidence path (dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence…), not against it. Counter, kept: the folds still wait for usage evidence from more than one project; the article supplies the argument, not the evidence.

3. GRANULARITY IS A CRITERION FOR WHEN A TOOL EARNS ITS PLACE — the article's one technical point. An operation exists to collapse a multi-step sequence the model would otherwise get wrong between the steps (link_artifact = artifact + fragment + edge, atomically, is exactly this). Read against the 6 constructor-plus-edge fold candidates: the question for each is not "are these two names?" but "does the model err BETWEEN the two calls?" — the multiple_parents defect (contain, then contain again) was such an error. This is a sharper test than orthogonality alone. Counter: the typed-helper rule already says a helper earns its place by a guard or a computation the generic call lacks; granularity is a third way to earn it, not a replacement.

═══ WHERE THE LINE IS QUESTIONABLE TODAY — candidates, in the spirit of the premise, none judged ═══
Places where reflow2 arguably does something the LLM does better, recorded so they can be looked at rather than argued from memory:
· gaps_to_prompts / gap_to_prompt: the graph phrasing a question for a human is speaking, not counting; the `rephrase_degraded` flag exists because the agent is expected to re-say it. Is the template the graph's job at all, or only the gap and its affected ids?
· graph_report_markdown: prose narration of state is what the where-am-i skill has the AGENT do in the reader's words; a markdown projection from the graph competes with that. (Anthony's own doctrine: views are pure projections; a renderer that fills in is a defect.)
· find_tools: a deterministic ranker choosing tools for a model that, per the article, reads all the declarations anyway. It exists for the latent surface and the corpus test; is it a crutch for a surface that is too large?
· propose_heal / propose_allocation: the graph proposing design changes. Structural arithmetic with the human deciding — inside the line — but worth saying so explicitly.
And the converse, where the LLM's weaknesses are caught (inside the line, working): tool choice between two doors (the rank ratchet), arithmetic on quantities (budget_report, closure), memory across sessions (the graph), its own confidence (measured vs asserted — extended to checksums the same day this was recorded).

═══ WHAT REFLOW2 SHOULD NOT DO ON THIS EVIDENCE ═══
Not build a second protocol surface (OpenAPI, GraphQL) for its own sake: the article's conclusion is that MCP won sociologically, and dec:the-mcp-surface-is-two-boundaries-not-one-medium already keeps the CONTRACT in the toolsnaps with transports as projections, so a non-MCP client (flo2's GraphQL edge, a CLI) is cheap when a consumer needs one and pointless before. dec:idea-mcp-has-no-openapi-and-reflow2-already-speaks-that-vocabulary stays open and separate.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
A. NOTHING — the doctrine already answers the premise; keep this as the record that the article was read. 
B. ADD GRANULARITY TO THE EARNS-ITS-PLACE TEST — when a fold candidate is judged, ask whether the model errs between the two calls; if yes, the folded single operation is the one that stays. Cheap: a sentence in the tool-pruning decision and the instrument. 
C. AUDIT THE FOUR CANDIDATES ABOVE against the three-party line, each as a finding with a measured instance or a note that none was found. 
D. RESTATE dec:three-party-checks AS A DESIGN RULE delivered on the capture skills, so the line is read at the moment a new capability is proposed rather than remembered.
properties.name: OPEN — does 'MCP is unnecessary' (Kellogg, 2025-04-27) change what reflow2 should or should not do, and where is the LLM/graph/human line questionable today?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill from Anthony's question, nothing promoted. Recorded as its own question rather than appended to dec:three-party-checks because that decision is settled and this asks whether an outside argument moves it (it does not); linked to it and to the prune idea, which the article's standardization point argues for.
